title: In an array where every number appears twice except two numbers that each appear once, find both single numbers using constant extra space. Explain how a distinguishing set bit splits the array into two groups.
shortTitle: Two Single Numbers (Find the Two Elements That Each Appear Once)
keyPoints: XOR all elements to get the combined XOR of the two single numbers.
The combined XOR has at least one set bit because the two singles are different.
Isolate the rightmost set bit using x & (-x), a classic two's complement idiom.
Split the array into two groups by that bit: one group per single number.
XOR each group separately to recover each single number.
Paired values fall into the same group and cancel within it.
Time complexity is O(n); space complexity is O(1).

s1_definition.oneliner: XOR everything to combine the two singles, isolate a differing bit, split into two groups by that bit, and XOR each group to recover each single.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Combined XOR** – XOR-ing the entire array gives the XOR of the two unpaired numbers (`x = a ^ b`).
- **Differing bit** – since `a != b`, `x` has at least one set bit; isolate the rightmost with `x & (-x)`.
- **Partitioning** – split every element into two groups by whether the differing bit is set or not.
- **Recovery** – XOR each group separately; paired values cancel within their group, leaving one single in each.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time (two passes), O(1) space.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, two orphan reconciliation entries slipped through unmatched while everything else is paired. XOR-ing all codes gives the combined fingerprint of the two orphans. Rajesh picks one bit where they differ, sorts every code into two buckets by that bit, and XOR-ing each bucket reveals the orphan in it.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
Array: [101, 202, 303, 404, 101, 303]

Step 1: XOR all → 101^202^303^404^101^303 = 202^404 = 342

Step 2: Rightmost set bit of 342
  342 = 101010110
  -342 = ...complement...
  342 & (-342) = 10 = 2

Step 3: Split by bit 2
  Group A (bit set):   202(10), 303(10), 303(10) → 202^303^303 = 202
  Group B (bit unset): 101(00), 404(00), 101(00) → 101^404^101 = 404

Result: [202, 404]

┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Combined XOR reveals differing bit      │
│  Split → each single in its own group    │
│  Pairs cancel within each group          │
│  XOR per group → recover each single     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Two Single Numbers extends the basic XOR trick to the case where two elements each appear once. XOR-ing the entire array cancels all pairs and leaves the combined XOR of the two singles. Because the two singles are different numbers, this combined value has at least one set bit, and any such bit is a bit where the two singles differ.

Isolate one such bit, conventionally the rightmost using the `x & (-x)` idiom from two's complement, and use it as a splitter. Pass over the array a second time and route each number into one of two groups depending on whether that bit is set. The two singles are guaranteed to land in different groups, while every paired value still cancels within whichever group it lands in. XOR-ing each group independently reveals the two singles.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh uses this when two reconciliation entries, rather than one, are left unmatched while everything else is paired. XOR-ing all codes gives their combined fingerprint, isolating a differing bit partitions the codes into two buckets, and each orphan is revealed by XOR. The whole operation takes O(n) time and O(1) space.

The key interview insight is the distinguishing-bit split. The `x & (-x)` idiom isolates the rightmost set bit, and understanding why it works requires knowing two's complement. Being able to explain the split, the pairing guarantee, and the rightmost-bit idiom shows bit-level reasoning under a space constraint.

Remember one sentence: XOR everything to combine the two singles, isolate a differing bit to split them into separate groups, and XOR each group to recover each single.
